## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Fix case normalization before merging so the new `Cache.set` method works with the cache’s case-insensitive lookups.

## Changes
The pull request adds `Cache.set`, increases the default TTL from 60 to 300 seconds, and adds tests for reads after writes, the default TTL constant, and expiration.

## Critical

- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Lowercase keys before storing entries — After `cache.set("Alpha", 1)`, `cache.get("Alpha")` returns `None` because `set` stores `"Alpha"` and `get` looks up `"alpha"`. — Mixed-case writes also leave entries that expiration cleanup can never remove.

## Important

(none)

## Suggestions

- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Expire entries at their deadline — Exactly 300 seconds after a default cache writes `"alpha"`, `get("alpha")` still returns the stored value. The new setter records the deadline, and `app/cache.py:21` checks it with a strict `<` comparison. — A read at the deadline can serve a value whose configured lifetime has elapsed. — Fix: Use `<=` at `app/cache.py:21`.
- tests/test_cache.py:18 — tests — Test expiry with the default constructor — If a default-constructed cache uses a 60-second TTL, `test_default_ttl_is_five_minutes` still passes because it only reads `Cache.DEFAULT_TTL`. — The suite leaves the five-minute default unprotected against regressions in how the constructor applies it.
